metadata.description: Fraud-detection OLTP over Bolt/TCP+TLS via the official Neo4j driver: load a seeded fraud graph, detect EXACTLY the planted fraud, and sustain extreme-concurrency SSI.

notes: storage.bytes_fsynced is a proxy: the WAL on-disk byte count (every committed WAL byte is fsynced before commit acknowledgement), not a directly-observed fsync counter.
Throughput window is the detection workload's ops over server uptime (a coarse proxy); latency percentiles + abort rate are measured by the drivers (GRAPHUS_STATS).
Live measurement of graphus-server over 4.000s uptime; CPU is the server's cumulative since-boot usage (the process is dedicated to this workload), RSS is sampled from the live process.

COMMITTED BASELINE (rmp #256; re-baselined under #673 when the production-realistic index/constraint schema was added, and again under #682 when a RELATIONSHIP KEY on TRANSFER.tx_id was added): the fast-profile reference run for the regression gate. The #682 re-baseline is legitimate on two structural axes — (1) the extra globally-unique tx_id string property on every TRANSFER grows the on-disk store (376832 -> 442368 bytes), and (2) the scan-based RELATIONSHIP KEY uniqueness check marks all live relationships as SIREAD, enlarging each writer's read footprint and raising the SSI abort rate (0.4741 -> 0.7667) while the no-lost-update invariant still holds. Only STABLE STRUCTURAL metrics (storage bytes/pages, operation count, abort-rate band) are compared against it; CPU/RAM/latency/throughput are machine-variant and are NOT gated (see baseline_cmp). Recorded on linux/x86_64.
